description: We are Team CMS Senior from Lahore, Pakistan, in South Asia. We compete in robotics, coding and STEM competitions, and every one of them has been fully self-funded. We do everything ourselves, from code and building hardware to design and presenting our work. We believe in being honest about every resource, AI tool and technology we use. What drives us is curiosity, the urge to achieve more, and the ambition to excel in every field. Our team comprises of highschoolers and young graduates.
summary:
A farmer in Punjab chooses what to plant the way their grandparents did, but the weather has changed. Underground water is running low, monsoon rains are harder to predict and heatwaves come earlier. NASA satellites measure all of this, but most farmers never see it. Khet-uz-Zaman changes that, so a village farmer in South Asia gets the same quality of advice as a farmer in the United States.

Khet-uz-Zaman is a website that helps farmers plan which crops to grow on the same field, season after season. A farmer finds their field on a map, enters soil type and water source, picks what matters most (income, soil health, saving water or low weather risk) and chooses today’s climate or a hotter, drier future. Using NASA data on rainfall, temperature, soil moisture, crop water use and underground water, it suggests three 3-year crop plans scored for water, soil, income and risk. Farmers can change any crop and see the scores update instantly.

It also offers a map comparing South Asia and the USA, a weather dashboard, and simple farming lessons with every science word explained, in English, Urdu, Hindi, Bengali and Punjabi. An AI helper answers questions and checks crop photos, providing voice assistance as well. Landlords can plan work, see all farms on one screen, organise farmer teams and schedule water supply turns without visiting every field.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Khet-uz-Zaman is a website that helps farmers decide which crops to grow on the same field, season after season. It uses NASA satellite data so the advice fits the farmer's own land and weather.

FEATURES

  1. My Farm: The farmer finds their field on a map, or adds it themselves. They choose their soil type, where their water comes from, up to two goals (more income, healthier soil, saving water or less weather risk), and today's climate or a hotter, drier future.
  2. Crop Plans: The website makes three 3-year crop plans. Each plan gets a score for water, soil, income and weather risk. The best plan is marked in green. Farmers can change any crop, copy or reset a plan, and see a month-by-month timeline.
  3. Map: Shows South Asia and the USA side by side as a colour heat map or a real satellite picture. Tap any spot to see details.
  4. Weather and Climate: Shows today's weather, the last 30 days, the whole year, rain compared with how much water crops need, daily temperatures, water in the soil, and changes in underground water.
  5. Season Calendar: Shows when each crop is planted and harvested.
  6. Learn: Simple lessons on the water cycle, crop roots, how beans and lentils add nitrogen to soil, and why changing crops is better than growing the same one. Every science word is explained, with AI-generated video tutorials (labelled as AI-generated).
  7. Farm Support: An AI helper that answers farming questions and can look at photos of crops. It warns that AI answers can be wrong.
  8. Landlord Planner: For owners of many farms. Weekly, monthly and yearly plans, one screen showing all land, crops, water and risk, farmer teams, and planning whose turn it is to use canal water.
  9. Five languages: English, Urdu, Hindi, Bengali and Punjabi.

NASA DATA WE USE

NASA POWER: temperature, humidity, wind and sunlight.

GPM IMERG: rainfall.

SMAP: how wet the soil is.

ECOSTRESS: how much water crops use.

GRACE/GRACE-FO: changes in underground water.

MODIS, Landsat and SRTM (through NASA Worldview): satellite pictures and land height.

Our prototype uses approximate sample values based on NASA records. Connecting live NASA data is our next step.

TOOLS WE USED

HTML, CSS and JavaScript to build the website in VS Code. Netlify to deploy it. NASA Worldview for satellite maps. Claude (by Anthropic) helped write code and translations; our team checked everything. Claude and Google Gemini run the AI helper.

IMPACT

A farmer in a small village gets the same quality of advice as a farmer in the USA. That means fewer failed crops, healthier soil and less wasted water. We are bridging the gap and taking steps towards standardized farming practices.

CREATIVITY

We are not just putting forward a bunch of tools or features, we're trying to create impact locally and turn this into something real. Our website can be used by the Government for monitoring and issuing advisories or disaster warnings. We are pitching a possible startup for long-term use. The tools and features on our website speak for themselves, especially the "Future Deployments" tab.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Farmers with limited access to the internet, being honest about our data and AI use.
